name: French with a final-syllable stress mark

ancestors.notes: The same transcription as fr-FR, with a stress mark added.

stress.notes: The mark stands on the last full syllable of a word that is not a function word (Hirst & Di Cristo 1998: 196-197, Anderson 1982: 537, Tranel 1987: 194-200, Walker 2001: 181-182; each as reported by the English Wikipedia article 'French phonology', section Stress). Other analyses put the stress on the phrase or hold that French has no lexical stress (Féry 2017: 181), so this spec is opt-in and fr-FR stays unmarked. The mark is written before the syllable onset (IPA convention). cliticless_words is the closed class of function words that eSpeak NG 1.52 leaves without a primary mark inside a sentence (checked with `espeak-ng -v fr --ipa -q` in three frames); the words it does mark there (sept, huit, neuf, dix, six, si, donc, bien, mal) are not listed. eSpeak writes ˌ on avec, aussi, oui; this spec writes no secondary mark.

notes: A notation variant of fr-FR: the transcription is the fr-FR one (every table comes from fr-FR) and the only addition is a `stress` block, so it is opt-in: fr-FR and the regional French tags stay without stress marks, which keeps every existing French transcription unchanged. NOT MODELLED: phrase-level stress groups, secondary stress, the contrastive/emphatic initial accent, liaison-dependent shifts. Stress follows the written word, so a word such as a number before a vowel (six ans) is marked as in isolation.
